liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Loser** (2 reviews): Jerry's vocals on Loser are singled out as strong, with his lyrics accurate and him engaged, while Bob forgets words; Loser is good, but the band missed the jump during the jam [8][15]
- **Hey Pocky Way** (1 review): Opens laid back, with each note and beat well defined [10]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Bare-bones version with forgotten lyrics; picks up midway with percussion, but the jam tells no clear story [11]
- **Iko Iko** (1 review): The start of Iko Iko is the weirdest this listener has heard [18]
- **A Little Light** (1 review): The first A Little Light is rough but magnificent, hinting at big potential for future exploratory jams [8]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-02-07.149698.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 160 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1989-02-07.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.106929.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 152 min; rated 2.4/5 by 5 [2]
- **gd1989-02-07.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.32543.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 155 min; rated 3.14/5 by 7 [6]
- **gd89-02-07.sbd.wiley.9202.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 154 min; rated 2.83/5 by 12 [7]. Said about its sound: The soundboard source runs slow and needs pitch correction; Listener finds the sound thick, warm and punchy, though agrees tape speed needs adjusting; A droning, wavering sound, like a failing record, runs through the first set of this source [9][10][11][16]

## Around the show

- Listener from Chicago found the venue packed and the scene wild, far from the mellow California vibe expected [12]
- Defends the review page's personal stories as an intimate window into what happened around Dead shows [14]
- Speakers filled the hallways, and the intimate hall with hometown fans let Phil's bombs be appreciated [19]
- A Mardi Gras parade took place during Iko Iko [2]
- A Mardi Gras parade took place during Iko Iko [6]
- Sees the first set as slow and methodical; a decent show overall [15]
- Finds the show scattered and enormously inconsistent [16]
- Great Miller sound, but only average compared to the standout shows of 1989 [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-02-07.149698.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  April 22 2020; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) [1]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; several sets of masters were combined to complete the show [1]
- **gd1989-02-07.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.106929.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-X90/Dolby B) [2]
- **gd1989-02-07.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.32543.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK MA-X90) D [6]. Also: Made from cassettes from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker, with a seamless transition between discs 2 and 3 [6]
- **gd89-02-07.sbd.wiley.9202.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>MC>DAT>CDR [7]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Henry J. Kaiser Convention Center - February 7, 1989](https://www.dead.net/show/february-7-1989) [21]
- Poster by Kirsten Michel: [1989-02-07 Henry J. Kaiser Convention Center, Oakland, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1989-02-07-henry-j-kaiser-convention-center-oakland-ca-usa/) [22]
